# `doc-comment-style`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: official · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a doc comment that merely repeats information already supplied by the
declaration name.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Documentation is most valuable when it explains contracts, invariants,
ownership, or surprising behavior instead of narrating the identifier.

## When it fires

Enable it when maintaining API documentation quality; short obvious declarations
need not acquire filler prose.

It reads the first sentence of the comment, which may run over several lines,
and fires only when that sentence starts with the declaration's name and says
nothing else: the name alone (`/// EMCON`, `/// Bar.`), or the name followed by
at most a few filler words (articles, `is`, `type`, `function`, `returns`) and
the name's own words, possibly inflected (`/// Parser type.`,
`/// renderFrame renders the frame.`). A first sentence that adds anything
(`/// Shaper that uses Harfbuzz.`, `/// Index into nodes.`,
`/// Mutex is a synchronization primitive.`) is documentation.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
/// renderFrame renders the frame.
pub fn renderFrame() void {}
```

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/#Doc-Comment-Guidance>
